newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close low on blue chip falls.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close low on blue chip falls.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower on Wednesday due to declines in two highly capitalised blue chips, while overall trading, despite being positive, was limited due to low liquidity, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.49 points down at 609.52. Development Finance fell 50 cents to 269.50 and John Keells Holdings two rupees to 195.

"The market will continue to remain positive since better corporate results are seen in the last quarter of 1996, and first quarter of 1997," said Sarinda Unamboowe, general manager of brokerage John Keells.
Any substantial rise in volume, however, will be seen only if the all share goes beyond 700 points, because it is the level at which investors could take significant profits, he said.
Turnover was 51.2 million rupees on 1.5 million shares, led by 272,600 Ceylon Brewery, 75,900 Development Finance and 10,000 John Keells Holdings.
"Since liquidity is a problem you cannot get lines without paying premiums, which some investors are not willing to do," said a broker at Jardine Fleming.
Foreign buying amounted to 23.34 million rupees, and selling was 17.8 million.
